# 新論-漢-桓譚 / tls

**ID:** KR3j0192
**Date (file):** 2017-01-15 17:23:51
**Base edition:** CBETA
**Categories:** 10,選集

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Originally a 17-*juàn* philosophical and political treatise by the Western-Hàn / Wáng-Mǎng / Eastern-Hàn transition scholar [桓譚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A1%93%E8%AD%9A) (Huán Tán). The complete text was lost in the medieval period; the present recension is a fragment-reconstruction from quotations in classical and medieval sources, principally as gathered by Yán Kějūn 嚴可均 in his *Quán shànggǔ sāndài Qín-Hàn sānguó liùcháo wén* (early 19th c.), where it occupies juàn 93–95 of the *Quán Hòu Hàn wén* section. The KRP source text is drawn from this reconstruction.

The *Suí shū jīngjí zhì · Rújiā* records the *Huánzǐ xīn lùn* in 17 *juàn*, compiled by the Eastern-Hàn *Liùān chéng* Huán Tán; the old and new *Táng shū* records agree. The *Hòu Hàn shū* biography records: Tán's *zì* was Jūnshān, a Pèiguó Xiāngrén; *láng* under Chéngdì; under Āidì and Píngdì, his rank did not exceed *láng*; under Wáng Mǎng, *Zhǎngyuè dàfū*. The text accounting for [KR3j0192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0192) in the krp-titles index thus refers to this reconstructed fragment-collection.

**Abstract**

The *Xīn lùn* is the major philosophical work of [桓譚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A1%93%E8%AD%9A) (Huán Tán), one of the most important rationalist and historical-critical thinkers of the Western-Hàn / Eastern-Hàn transition. Huán's principal positions — preserved in the surviving fragments — include:

1. *Anti-prognostication (chènwěi) critique*. Huán was one of the leading Hàn opponents of the *chènwěi* (prognostication-apocrypha) literature that grew up around the Hàn classics. His refusal to confirm the *chèn* predictions in front of Guāngwǔdì 光武帝 led to his demotion and effective exile — a famous incident in Eastern-Hàn intellectual history.
2. *Yángshén / xíngshén dispute*. Huán's discussions of the candle-and-flame analogy — that consciousness (*shén*) depends on the body (*xíng*) as a flame depends on the wax — were the foundational early-Chinese articulation of the materialist position in the *xíngshén* (body-spirit) debate. Wáng Chōng 王充's *Lùn héng* engages directly with Huán's position; Fàn Zhěn's 范縝 *Shén miè lùn* in the 5th–6th c. develops it.
3. *Historical criticism*. Huán's commentary on Hàn institutions and politics — including his observations on the Wáng Mǎng usurpation, of which he was an eyewitness — was an important source for Hàn historiography.
4. *Western-Hàn-style cosmology*. Huán was a contemporary and critic of Liú Xiàng / Liú Xīn's bibliographic and cosmological project. The fragments preserve his alternative positions.

Dating. Huán Tán's career bridges the Western-Hàn (under Chéngdì, Āidì, Píngdì), Wáng Mǎng's interregnum (where he served as *Zhǎngyuè dàfū*), and the early Eastern-Hàn (where his refusal of the *chènwěi* led to his demotion under Guāngwǔdì). Composition of the *Xīn lùn* is conventionally dated to the late Wáng Mǎng / early Eastern-Hàn period. *NotBefore* 25 CE (Guāngwǔdì restoration), *notAfter* 56 CE (Huán's approximate death date; the *Hòu Hàn shū* records he died of distress shortly after his demotion).

Textual transmission. The work was complete in 17 *juàn* through the Suí and Táng. The Sòng catalogues already record only fragments. Yán Kějūn's early-19th-c. reconstruction is the standard modern fragment-collection; *Sūn Píngyí* 孫馮翼's *Wèn jīngtáng* compilation is an earlier (Qīng) recovery; Zhū Qiānzhī 朱謙之's modern critical edition gathers further fragments.
